stages.label: Learn

blocks.title: Analogue versus digital
blocks.text: Real sound is continuous. To digitise it, a computer samples the wave at regular intervals and stores measurements as binary.

blocks.title: Sample rate
blocks.text: Sample rate is the number of samples measured per second, in hertz (Hz). More samples can capture more detail.

blocks.title: Bit depth
blocks.text: Bit depth is the number of bits available for each sample's amplitude; more bits allow finer amplitude representation.

blocks.title: Raw mono sound
blocks.text: Raw bits = sample rate × seconds × bit depth. Divide by eight for bytes. Channels, headers and compression can change real file size.

blocks.title: Visual model · Sound, Sampling, Bit Depth and File Sizes
blocks.caption: Sample rate controls how often measurements are taken; bit depth controls their precision.

blocks.title: Worked model · A mono clip uses 10 samples per second, lasts 5 seconds and uses 8 bits per sample. Find the raw size.
blocks.text: Write the formula: rate × duration × bit depth. 10 samples/s × 5 seconds = 50 samples. 50 × 8 = 400 bits. 400 ÷ 8 = 50 bytes (raw, mono, uncompressed).

items: sample rate — Number of samples taken per second.
bit depth — Number of bits representing each sample.
